sources.entry: Think Bayes: Bayesian Statistics in Python by Allen B. Downey

summary.name: Think Bayes 2e
summary.one_liner: Think Bayes 2nd edition is a free introductory book by Allen B. Downey that teaches Bayesian statistics using Python code and discrete approximations instead of mathematical notation.
use_cases: building Bayesian regression or logistic regression models
running Monte Carlo sampling with PyMC
practicing with exercises in Jupyter notebooks
summary.what_it_does: The book introduces Bayesian statistics using computational methods, replacing integrals with summations and distribution operations with loops or array operations. The second edition adds a new Chapter 1 on conditional probability (using the Linda the Banker problem and General Social Survey data) and new chapters on survival analysis, linear regression, logistic regression, conjugate priors, Monte Carlo sampling with PyMC, and approximate Bayesian computation. All code was rewritten with NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas. Each chapter has a companion Jupyter notebook with text, runnable code, and exercises, which can be run locally or on Colab. The code is in a GitHub repository.
notable: Uses Python code instead of calculus-based math notation
Free online read with Jupyter notebook per chapter
